subject.title: fix: Node allowlist writeback can restore revoked exec approvals

question: Should exec-side allow-always and metadata writes be skipped whenever the approvals file changed after policy evaluation, or may they merge into the latest approvals file under the new lock?
rationale: The PR fixes full-file stale overwrite behavior but changes the permanent approval semantics for in-flight allow-always decisions, which is a security-boundary choice rather than a pure mechanical repair.

options.title: Require evaluated freshness
options.body: Propagate the evaluated approvals hash into exec-side locked writes and skip persistence when the file changed after evaluation; this matches the admin-wins framing of the linked security issue.

options.title: Accept merge-into-current writes
options.body: Keep the current merge-under-lock behavior, but document and test that in-flight allow-always decisions may persist into a concurrently updated approvals file.

options.title: Pause for owner rewrite
options.body: Hold this branch until an exec/security owner rewrites the persistence contract and proof plan.

recommendation.title: Require evaluated freshness
recommendation.body: Propagate the evaluated approvals hash into exec-side locked writes and skip persistence when the file changed after evaluation; this matches the admin-wins framing of the linked security issue.
